skill.name: using-git-worktrees
skill.description: Creates isolated Git worktrees for feature work, verifies ignore rules, runs setup, and reports a clean baseline before implementation.
skill.summary: Guides isolated Git worktree setup for safer feature development.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown fences, documented worktree paths, and stderr redirects. I found no prompt injection or data exfiltration intent. The main risks are automatic project command execution and an automatic commit step.

remediation.suggestion: Ask for confirmation before running installs, builds, or tests in untrusted repositories. Prefer lockfile-based commands and script-reduced modes when available.
Show the .gitignore change and ask before committing. Allow users to continue without a commit when policy requires it.
Create ~/.config worktree directories only after user selection. Report the final absolute path before running setup commands.

static_findings.snippet: **If found:** Use that directory. If both exist, `.worktrees` wins.

semantic_findings.title: Automatic Project Setup Can Execute Untrusted Code
semantic_findings.description: The skill tells agents to auto-detect project files and run installs, builds, and tests. In untrusted repositories, these commands can execute repository-controlled scripts.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The workflow explicitly says to run setup and test commands. Package lifecycle hooks and tests are common arbitrary code execution paths.

semantic_findings.title: Automatic Commit Without Confirmation
semantic_findings.description: The skill instructs the agent to add a .gitignore entry and commit the change before creating a worktree. This can modify repository history without explicit approval.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited steps directly tell the agent to change .gitignore and commit it. The risk is workflow integrity, not data exfiltration.

content.value_statement: Feature work can disrupt an active checkout or hide baseline failures. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through safer Git worktree setup.
actual_capabilities: Checks for existing .worktrees or worktrees directories before asking for a location.
Reads CLAUDE.md for a worktree directory preference when no directory exists.
Verifies project-local worktree directories are listed in .gitignore.
Creates a new Git worktree and branch with git worktree add.
Runs common setup and test commands based on project files.
Reports the created worktree path and baseline test result.
limitations: Requires an existing Git repository with the git command available.
Package installation and tests can execute project-defined code.
Does not choose a worktree location when project conventions are ambiguous.
Does not clean up completed worktrees; a separate workflow is referenced.

use_cases.title: Start feature work safely
use_cases.description: Create a separate workspace before changing code while preserving the current checkout.

use_cases.title: Prepare plan implementation
use_cases.description: Move approved implementation work into an isolated branch with setup and baseline checks.

use_cases.title: Standardize team worktrees
use_cases.description: Follow consistent directory and .gitignore rules across repositories.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Feature Worktree
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an isolated Git worktree for feature/<name>. Follow project conventions and ask before choosing a new location.

prompt_templates.title: Use Existing Repository Rules
prompt_templates.prompt: Check this repository for worktree directory conventions, verify ignore rules, then create a worktree for <branch>.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare Before Implementation
prompt_templates.prompt: Before implementing this approved plan, create a clean worktree, run setup, and report baseline test status.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Worktree Readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the repository worktree setup, identify missing safety steps, and prepare an isolated workspace only after approval.

output_examples.input: Create a worktree for feature authentication.
output: Verified the ignore rule for project-local worktrees.
Created the feature workspace and confirmed the baseline tests pass.

output_examples.input: No worktree directory exists in this repository.
output_examples.output: The skill asks the user to choose a project-local or global worktree location before creating anything.
The skill reports the failure and asks whether to investigate or continue with the known failing baseline.

best_practices: Verify ignore rules before creating project-local worktrees.
Ask before running setup commands in repositories you do not trust.
Record the final worktree path and baseline status before implementation.
anti_patterns: Creating worktrees in project folders that are not ignored.
Running installs or tests blindly in untrusted repositories.
Proceeding after failing baseline tests without user approval.

faq.question: What problem does this skill solve?
faq.answer: It creates isolated Git workspaces so feature work does not disturb the current checkout.

faq.question: Does it require Git worktree support?
faq.answer: Yes. The repository must use Git, and the git command must be available.

faq.question: Does it choose the worktree directory automatically?
faq.answer: It uses existing conventions first, checks CLAUDE.md next, and asks when the location is ambiguous.

faq.question: Can setup commands be risky?
faq.answer: Yes. Installs, builds, and tests may execute project-defined scripts in untrusted repositories.

faq.question: Does it clean up old worktrees?
faq.answer: No. The skill references a separate finishing workflow for cleanup after development is complete.

faq.question: Can Claude Code and Codex use it?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
